Prevention: Always remove and destroy any remaining old plants at the end of the growing season.
Crop rotation will also reduce cases of leaf miner.
The host range is extensive but plant crop unaffected by leaf miner.
Mulch, such as black plastic, can help reduce fly emergence from the pupae in the soil.
Monitoring: Check for tiny row of little white eggs on the leaves (especially at the tip).
The characteristic long trailing mines are very obvious.
Look for small flies that look like house flies.
Yellow-sticky traps can be placed on the edges of fields to monitor adult activity and detect movement.
Direct Control: Neem preparation concentration depending on formulation.
Cyromazine (Trigard) ¼ to ½ tsp/ gal
Restrictions: Rotate chemical use (change chemical regularly) to prevent the build-up of resistant miners.
